elements.title: Organizational Structure
elements.content:
Organizational chart. Central top box: “Administrator / Deputy Administrator / Associate Administrator.”

Connected to the central leadership box:
- Left, by solid connector: “Chief Financial Officer” and “Chief Information Officer.”
- Left of those offices, connected by dotted lines indicating independent advisory or oversight organizations: “Advisory Groups—NAC & ASAP” and “Inspector General.”
- Right, by solid connector: “Office of Technology, Policy and Strategy.”
- Downward, by a solid vertical connector to the organizational structure below.

Left-side offices and support organizations connected to the lower organizational line:
- “Diversity & Equal Opportunity” — “Small Business Programs.”
- “STEM Engagement” — “Communications.”
- “International & Interagency Relations” — “Legislative & Intergovernmental Affairs.”
- “General Counsel.”

Mission Directorates and related offices connected to the lower organizational line:
- “Aeronautics Research Mission Directorate” — “Exploration Systems Development Mission Directorate.”
- “Science Mission Directorate” — “Space Operations Mission Directorate.”
- “Space Technology Mission Directorate” — “Mission Support Directorate.”
- “Chief Engineer” — “Chief, Safety & Mission Assurance.”
- “Chief Health & Medical Officer” — “Chief Scientist/Senior Climate Advisor.”

Research centers connected in the right-side hierarchy:
- “Ames Research Center” — “Johnson Space Center.”
- “Armstrong Flight Research Center” — “Kennedy Space Center.”
- “Glenn Research Center” — “Langley Research Center.”
- “Goddard Space Flight Center” — “Marshall Space Flight Center.”
- “Jet Propulsion Laboratory**” — “Stennis Space Center.”

The boxes are connected by solid lines unless otherwise noted. The chart’s lower central vertical line connects the Administrator/Deputy Administrator/Associate Administrator to the lower organizational structure. Horizontal connectors link paired offices and centers as shown above.

FY 2024 AGENCY FINANCIAL REPORT  NASA.GOV

Organizational Structure
MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
WELCOME TO NASA
The innovative, responsive, and dynamic nature of NASA’s work benefits from our highly leveraged relationships with 
and between Mission Directorates, Mission Support Offices, and Centers. This organizational model ensures that our 
leaders can take both a holistic and more narrowly focused approach to programmatic, operational, business, and safety 
management.5
The Administrator and senior officials lead NASA by providing top-level strategy, policy, and direction. NASA’s Office 
of the Chief Financial Officer leads the Agency’s budget, financial, and performance management processes. Mission 
Directorates and Mission Support Offices at Headquarters manage decisions on programmatic investments and guide 
operations of the Centers.
LEGEND
 **JET PROPULSON LABORATORY (JPL)
is a Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC) managed by the 
California Institute of Technology (Caltech) with oversight by the NASA Office of JPL 
Management and Oversight
Dotted lines indicate independent advisory or oversight organizations
NASA Advisory Council (NAC) | Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel (ASAP)
NASA’s Headquarters, located in Washington, DC, provides the overall guidance and direction to the Agency under the 
leadership of the Administrator. A skilled and diverse group of technical and business professionals conduct day-to-day 
activities throughout our nine Centers and multiple unique facilities.
